name: Relaxed states and Taylor relaxation
summary: Taylor relaxation finds minimum magnetic energy at fixed helicity, a constrained variational principle like maximum-entropy with conserved quantities, producing force-free states in reversed-field pinches and spheromaks.
breaks: Relaxation requires turbulent reconnection, not true thermal equilibrium; ergodic hypotheses are heuristic.

name: Debye–Hückel screening
summary: Debye shielding is the Debye–Hückel mean-field treatment of a Coulomb system in the canonical/grand canonical ensemble: linearized Poisson–Boltzmann gives the screened potential and the leading correlation free-energy correction.

name: Strongly coupled one-component plasma
summary: The one-component plasma is a classic liquid-state model with coupling Γ; its Monte Carlo/MD equation of state and freezing near Γ≈175 connect plasma physics to classical liquid theory.

name: Statistical mechanics in magnetic fields (Bohr–van Leeuwen)
summary: Classical equilibrium partition function is independent of B, so classical plasmas have no magnetization (Bohr–van Leeuwen); diamagnetic currents are cancelled by boundary orbits, with magnetic moment conservation tied to adiabatic invariants.
breaks: Applies to thermal equilibrium; nonequilibrium plasmas with adiabatic invariants show strong magnetic effects.

name: Non-Maxwellian tails and nonextensive statistics
summary: Space plasmas show kappa distributions with power-law tails, which some interpret via Tsallis nonextensive statistics; alternatively tails arise from acceleration and turbulence.
breaks: Tsallis interpretation is contested; kinetic acceleration models explain tails without it.

name: Gibbs entropy and velocity-space cascade
summary: Free-energy conservation in gyrokinetics combines entropy of fluctuations with field energy, and Landau-damped energy appears as fine-scale velocity structure; coarse-graining sets irreversible heating.

name: Degenerate electrons in HED matter
summary: Warm dense matter and ICF fuel compression involve partially degenerate Fermi gases; the Fermi energy versus temperature sets the degeneracy parameter, and Fermi-gas pressure limits compression.

name: Fermi degeneracy and ICF fuel
summary: ICF compresses fuel on a low adiabat, keeping it near-degenerate to minimise compression work; the adiabat parameter is the ratio of fuel pressure to Fermi pressure.

name: Radiation and blackbody in laser plasmas
summary: Radiation in hohlraums and hot plasmas is a Planck photon gas; indirect-drive ICF relies on x-ray bath near blackbody equilibrium and Stefan–Boltzmann scaling.

name: Plasmons and collective quanta
summary: Langmuir waves quantize as plasmons in degenerate electron gases, with the same plasma frequency and Bohm–Pines RPA treatment as in metals; Bose statistics of phonon-like modes applies.

name: Nonequilibrium stat mech and Vlasov kinetics
summary: Plasma kinetics is nonequilibrium statistical mechanics of a long-range-interacting gas: the Vlasov equation is the collisionless limit of the BBGKY hierarchy, with Fokker–Planck collisions as the weak-scattering closure.
map: \partial_t f+\mathbf v\cdot\nabla f+\tfrac{q}{m}(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)\cdot\partial_{\mathbf v}f=C[f]

name: Avalanches and critical gradient transport
summary: Profile stiffness above critical gradients and avalanche-like transport events in tokamaks are compared with sandpile SOC models; zonal flows resemble self-regulating shear.
breaks: Gyrokinetic turbulence has specific linear thresholds and fluid physics beyond sandpile rules.

name: Nonequilibrium cascades as driven steady states
summary: MHD turbulence is a driven dissipative steady state with a constant flux cascade through scales, comparable to scale-invariant nonequilibrium steady states studied in KPZ and driven-diffusive systems.
breaks: Energy cascades have no detailed-balance structure but also lack the exact stochastic-model solvability.

name: Self-organized criticality in substorms and flares
summary: Avalanche models of self-organized criticality have been applied to solar flares and magnetospheric substorms, whose power-law event statistics resemble sandpile avalanches.
breaks: Flare and substorm driving and loading are not clearly critical; MHD-based explanations compete.

name: Collisional transport and neoclassical theory
summary: Collisional transport coefficients in magnetized plasma follow from kinetic theory via Chapman–Enskog/Braginskii closures; neoclassical theory adds trapped-particle effects from toroidal geometry to random-walk diffusion estimates.

name: Plasma fundamentals and Boltzmann kinetics
summary: Plasma collision operators (Landau, Lenard–Balescu, Fokker–Planck) are the Coulomb-interaction versions of the Boltzmann collision integral, with a Coulomb logarithm cutoff set by Debye screening.

name: Boltzmann equation to Vlasov equation
summary: Vlasov is the Boltzmann equation with the collision term dropped and a self-consistent mean field added; the H-theorem fails for it, yet Landau damping gives effective irreversibility via phase mixing.
map: C[f]\to 0,\; \mathbf F\to q(\mathbf E[f]+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B[f])
breaks: Vlasov is time-reversible and conserves all Casimirs; damping is phase mixing, not entropy production.

name: Landau damping and the H-theorem
summary: Both explain relaxation of a distribution function; Boltzmann's is entropy-producing via collisions, Landau's is collisionless via resonant wave-particle energy exchange and phase mixing.
breaks: Landau damping conserves entropy and is reversible in principle; collisional H-theorem increases entropy.

name: Collisionless solar wind and Knudsen number
summary: Solar wind has large Knudsen number, so Boltzmann-equation exospheric models predict non-Maxwellian electron and ion distributions and heat flux, the origin of Parker-like kinetic closures beyond fluid theory.

name: X-ray Thomson scattering and FDT
summary: XRTS measures the dynamic structure factor of warm dense matter, which by the fluctuation–dissipation theorem encodes density response, temperature (detailed balance) and collective modes.

name: Conductivity, Kubo formula and Spitzer
summary: Plasma resistivity and transport coefficients can be derived from Kubo formulas, with Spitzer resistivity as the kinetic limit; Onsager symmetry constrains cross-coefficients such as thermoelectric terms.

name: Dielectric response, FDT and Landau damping
summary: The plasma dielectric function is a linear response function; its imaginary part gives Landau damping, and the FDT links it to thermal density fluctuations (dynamic structure factor, collective scattering).

name: Random-walk transport and Fokker–Planck
summary: Diffusive transport estimates, Fokker–Planck collision operators and quasilinear theory in plasmas treat turbulent or collisional scattering as a random walk in space or velocity.

name: Magnetic field-line and particle diffusion
summary: Charged-particle scattering by magnetic fluctuations gives pitch-angle diffusion and cosmic-ray transport; stochastic field lines yield Rechester–Rosenbluth diffusion, a random-walk with correlation length.

name: Stochastic acceleration and diffusive shock acceleration
summary: Fermi acceleration is a random-walk process in momentum and space; diffusive shock acceleration solves a diffusion–advection equation yielding a universal power-law spectrum.

name: Entropy production in collisionless plasma
summary: Entropy in weakly collisional plasma turbulence is cascaded to fine velocity-space scales (phase-space cascade) and dissipated by collisions, tied to Gibbs-entropy and fluctuation-theorem language.
breaks: Stochastic thermodynamics assumes Markovian baths; the plasma entropy cascade is deterministic Vlasov phase mixing.

name: Dynamo onset as a bifurcation
summary: The dynamo transition at critical magnetic Reynolds number resembles a continuous phase transition with a control parameter and symmetry-breaking order parameter (field amplitude), with saturation by Lorentz-force feedback.
breaks: No equilibrium free energy; the field has no thermal fluctuation-driven criticality.

name: Debye screening as mean-field theory
summary: Poisson–Boltzmann is a self-consistent mean-field theory, exact as the number of particles in a Debye sphere grows (plasma parameter large), analogous to the Ginzburg criterion.
breaks: Fails at strong coupling where Debye sphere holds few particles.

name: Landau theory of instability onset
summary: Plasma instabilities near threshold (two-stream, drift waves) show saturation amplitude equations resembling Landau–Ginzburg normal forms, with growth rate crossing zero like a control parameter.
breaks: Instabilities are nonequilibrium bifurcations without a free-energy functional.

name: RG and turbulence scaling
summary: Dynamic renormalization group was applied to stirred fluid and MHD turbulence (Forster–Nelson–Stephen, Fournier–Frisch), treating the cascade via scale elimination and fixed points.
breaks: Results are scheme-dependent and do not reproduce intermittency or anisotropic critical balance reliably.

name: 2D Coulomb systems and melting
summary: Two-dimensional dusty-plasma crystals melt via defect unbinding, discussed in KTHNY theory, a BKT-type two-step transition via dislocation and disclination unbinding.
breaks: Dusty plasmas are driven, dissipative and finite-size, with non-reciprocal forces.

name: Thermodynamic limits of energy devices
summary: Thermoelectrics, solar cells and batteries are bounded by second-law efficiency limits; ZT maps to a fraction of Carnot efficiency, and finite-time engine analysis applies.

name: Carnot bounds on solar cell efficiency
summary: Solar cells act as heat engines between the Sun and ambient temperature; the Shockley–Queisser limit and Landsberg/Carnot bounds follow from entropy generation in photon absorption and emission.
breaks: Photovoltaic conversion is quantum and band-gap limited, not a cyclic engine.

name: Photovoltaics as thermodynamic converters
summary: Detailed balance between absorbed and emitted blackbody radiation sets the SQ limit; thermodynamic treatments give ultimate limits for multijunction and hot-carrier cells.

name: Adsorption isotherms and chemical potential
summary: Langmuir and BET isotherms follow from equating the chemical potential of adsorbed and gas phases, i.e. a lattice-gas grand canonical calculation.

name: Electrochemical potential and battery voltage
summary: Cell voltage equals the Gibbs free-energy change per charge, with the open-circuit voltage from the chemical potential difference of lithium in the two electrodes.

name: Network science of biological regulation and spreading
summary: Scale-free and small-world network structure describes gene regulation, metabolic and neural networks, and epidemic spreading with vanishing thresholds.

name: Coherent backscattering and weak localization of waves
summary: Weak localization of light in turbid media produces coherent backscattering enhancement, which modifies diffuse optics and speckle statistics in tissue.
breaks: Strong localization is not reached in tissue; transport is nearly classical diffusion.

name: Percolation in composite electrodes and electrolytes
summary: Ionic and electronic conduction in composite battery electrodes and solid electrolytes depends on percolating pathways with critical thresholds and power-law conductivity.

name: Protein folding funnels and spin-glass landscapes
summary: Random-energy-model ideas and the principle of minimal frustration describe folding landscapes; glass transition temperature and funnel gap separate foldable sequences from glassy ones.
breaks: Evolved proteins are strongly non-random and minimally frustrated, unlike true spin glasses.

name: Statistical physics of neural computation
summary: Hopfield-network and replica methods from spin glasses are used to model neural memory, capacity and learning in neural biophysics.

name: Learning theory and protein structure inference
summary: Spin-glass landscape concepts and Boltzmann-machine/Potts inference (direct coupling analysis) link learning theory to protein folding and structure prediction.

name: Partition functions in transition-state theory
summary: Eyring transition-state theory writes rate constants as ratios of partition functions, and equilibrium constants follow from molecular partition functions.

name: Information-theoretic limits of quantum metrology
summary: Fisher information and Cramér–Rao bounds set measurement precision, mirroring maximum-entropy and information-geometry formulations of statistical mechanics.
breaks: Quantum Fisher information involves non-commuting observables with no classical-entropy counterpart.

name: Information limits in living systems
summary: Sensing precision, kinetic proofreading and gene regulation are bounded by mutual information and Landauer-type energy costs, using Shannon entropy and maximum entropy models.

name: Maximum entropy and information in image reconstruction
summary: Maximum-entropy priors and Shannon information underlie regularised image reconstruction and noise-limited image quality in CT and MRI.

name: Planck law and Earth's radiative balance
summary: Planck's blackbody spectrum and Stefan–Boltzmann law fix Earth's emission temperature; greenhouse absorption modifies the outgoing spectrum band by band.

name: Poisson counting statistics in emission imaging
summary: Radioactive decay counts are Poisson fluctuations, so SPECT and PET image noise scales as 1/√N, which governs time-of-flight gains.

name: Active and driven matter in living systems
summary: Exclusion processes, KPZ growth and active-matter nonequilibrium steady states model molecular traffic, tissue growth, bacterial colonies and collective cell motion.

name: Self-organized criticality in earthquakes
summary: Gutenberg–Richter power-law earthquake statistics and stick-slip fault models such as Burridge–Knopf and OFC are the standard examples of self-organized criticality and avalanche dynamics.
breaks: Real faults show characteristic-earthquake and aftershock correlations not captured by simple SOC models.

name: Vlasov-Boltzmann kinetics of charged beams
summary: Beam distributions evolve by Vlasov/Fokker–Planck equations in phase space, as in collisionless kinetic theory; Liouville's theorem underlies emittance conservation and cooling is a Fokker–Planck process.
breaks: Beams are far from equilibrium, with long-range space-charge and no collision-driven thermalization.

name: From Boltzmann kinetics to atmospheric fluid equations
summary: Chapman–Enskog reduction of the Boltzmann equation gives the Navier–Stokes transport coefficients used in atmospheric models; mean free path sets the continuum validity.

name: Onsager reciprocity and thermoelectric transport
summary: Seebeck and Peltier coefficients are related by Onsager reciprocity (Kelvin relation), and ZT follows from the matrix of transport coefficients constrained by the second law.

name: Fluctuation-dissipation limits on sensor noise
summary: Thermal noise in SQUIDs, resonators and magnetometers is tied to dissipation by the fluctuation–dissipation theorem (Johnson–Nyquist), setting sensitivity floors.

name: Langevin dynamics of tethered molecules
summary: Optical-tweezer bead and molecule dynamics are overdamped Langevin processes; force spectroscopy, Kramers escape and diffusion analyses use Fokker–Planck theory.

name: Kramers rate theory and reaction rates
summary: Barrier-crossing rates in solution follow Kramers theory, interpolating between transition-state theory and diffusion-limited regimes with friction.
breaks: Kramers theory assumes a single reaction coordinate with Markovian friction.

name: Hasselmann stochastic climate model
summary: Slow climate variability is modelled as an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, with fast weather as noise forcing the slow ocean and ice variables.
breaks: Weather noise is not strictly white and the system lacks detailed balance.

name: Diffusion and speckle in diffuse optics
summary: Photon transport in tissue reduces to a diffusion equation from random walks; diffusing-wave spectroscopy and Doppler/speckle techniques probe Brownian motion and blood flow.

name: Biophysics as stochastic thermodynamics
summary: Cellular sensing, motors and information processing are analysed by entropy production and thermodynamic uncertainty relations, linking precision to dissipation.

name: Fluctuation theorems for molecular machines
summary: Molecular motors and folding transitions operate far from equilibrium at kT scale; entropy production and Jarzynski/Crooks relations quantify their dissipation and free energies.

name: Dissipation cost of kinetic proofreading and sensing
summary: Energy dissipation buys accuracy in proofreading and sensing; entropy production bounds error rates and information rates.

name: Pulling experiments verify Jarzynski and Crooks
summary: Optical-tweezer unfolding of RNA hairpins verified Jarzynski and Crooks relations, recovering equilibrium free energies from nonequilibrium work distributions.

name: Lattice-gas models of adsorbate ordering
summary: Adsorbed monolayers map onto Ising lattice gases, with ordering transitions and surface reconstructions in Ising, Potts and universality classes; kinetic Monte Carlo models catalytic kinetics.

name: Tipping points and bifurcations in climate
summary: Ice-albedo and AMOC bistability resemble Landau free-energy double wells with first-order jumps and hysteresis, and critical slowing down serves as an early-warning signal.
breaks: Climate is driven and dissipative with no free energy to minimise.

name: Polymer scaling and coarse-graining of biomolecules
summary: Renormalization-group scaling gives polymer exponents for unfolded chains, and coarse-grained models of proteins use the same logic of eliminating fast degrees of freedom.

name: Fluctuating membranes and 2D defect physics
summary: Two-dimensional membranes and the hexatic/crystalline phases share 2D melting and defect-unbinding physics, plus thermal-undulation renormalisation of bending rigidity.
breaks: Membranes have out-of-plane fluctuations and fluid lipid order, so BKT applies only to in-plane ordered layers.
